reasoning_traces.think:
The intrinsic dimension (ID) estimator leverages a Bayesian mixture model of K Pareto distributions to infer heterogeneous ID values across player movements. Each observation is assigned to a latent manifold with its own ID d_k, where d_k ~ Pareto(1, d_k). This formulation arises from the assumption that local density is approximately constant, allowing the ratio of second-to-first nearest neighbor distances to follow a Pareto distribution. The model incorporates enhancements such as truncated Gamma priors on d_k and repulsive priors to avoid redundant components. In GSI, this framework is adapted to predict EPA by treating ID as a proxy for motion unpredictability. In GSE, it supports situational reasoning by identifying play phases through ID trajectory shifts. The method assumes spatial separation of manifolds and independence of observations, which may fail when motion is highly correlated or dense. Temporal dependencies in tracking data violate the independence assumption, necessitating extensions like Hidden Markov Models for accurate modeling.
